subject: lincomb prediction for multiple likelihood example

messages.author: bb0d51bd5af5ac0d
messages.subject: lincomb prediction for multiple likelihood example
parts:
Hi All,

I'm trying to get the predicted value of y1, y2, y3 for the example modeling 3 likelihood together with LMC(https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-manipula.html):

y1(s)=α1+z1(s)+e1(s)y2(s)=α2+λ1z1(s)+z2(s)+e2(s)y3(s)=α3+λ2z1(s)+λ3z2(s)+z3(s)+e3(s),
form <- y ~ 0 + intercept1 + intercept2 + intercept3 + 
  f(s1, model = spde) + f(s2, model = spde) + 
  f(s3, model = spde) + 
  f(s12, copy = "s1", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper) + 
  f(s13, copy = "s1", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper) + 
  f(s23, copy = "s2", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper) 
result <- inla(form, rep('gaussian', 3), 
  data = inla.stack.data(stack), 
  control.family = list(hyper.eps, hyper.eps, hyper.eps), 
  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack)),
  control.mode = list(theta = theta.ini, restart = TRUE),
  control.inla = list(int.strategy = 'eb'))

The example in the link above showed how to extract for each single random effect prediction(for z' s) but not the linear combination with λ's and z's.
I'm trying to get how to make a lincomb with all the random factors for predicting y's(instead of z's) here when setting up for INLA. 

Anyone could help? 

Many thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] lincomb prediction for multiple likelihood example
parts:
if you request s12, say, in the lincomb, then this term include the
lambda_1 term as well, so to predict y3, you can do

inla.make.lincomb(intercept3=1,
s13=1,
s23=1)

which is the sum of their first components. of,course, you would like
to make s13 = v, a vector of its length, with like one 1 and rest 0,
to extract a spesific component.

H

Thanks for the answer!
According to the example in book, posterior mean for z1 is A1 %*% result$summary.random$s1$mean. 
To make it simple, if I want to predict y1,i.e., I want (posterior mean of intercept1) + (posterior mean for z1) . Do you mean I can put lincomb = (intercept1 = v1, s1 =v2)  in the above inla function? where v1 and v2 are 0/1 vectors with ones on the right corresponding index position for intercept1 and s1.  once I get the lincomb effect, then do the A1%*%  to lincomb effect to project it. Does that sound right?

If I have some covariates in the formula beside intercepts, say x, I just do lincomb = (intercept1 = v1, x = vx,  s1 =v2), with x values on the right position within the long vector vx?
